strategies.name: Baseline Sequential All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Performs 16 dependent all-reduce operations sequentially with interleaved local scaling operations (multiply by a[r]/W, then divide by a[r]). Each all-reduce is a separate dispatch. 16 all-reduce dispatches plus local compute between each. Represents the reference implementation with no optimization—maximum latency but simplest structure.

strategies.name: Fused Local-Op Batched All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Pre-compute all scaling coefficients and fuse multiple (scale, divide) pairs into vectorized operations between all-reduces, reducing loop overhead. Still 16 all-reduce dispatches but with optimized local computation using tensor operations instead of per-shard loops. Trades memory allocation (temporary buffers) for reduced Python interpreter overhead in local ops.

strategies.name: Pipelined All-Reduce with Overlapped Compute
strategies.desc: Launch all-reduce on one buffer while computing local scaling operations on another buffer from the previous iteration, using double-buffering to hide computation latency behind communication. Still 16 all-reduce operations but attempts to overlap compute and communication phases. Requires careful buffer management to maintain dependencies while enabling pipeline parallelism.

strategies.name: Chunked Hierarchical All-Reduce Tree
strategies.desc: Split the 16 iterations into hierarchical groups (e.g., 4 groups of 4), performing intra-group all-reduces first, then inter-group aggregation to reduce the number of global synchronization points. Potentially 8-12 dispatches instead of 16 by batching operations within subtrees. Trades algorithmic complexity for fewer network round-trips at world_size=224.

strategies.name: Reduced-Iteration Algebraic Simplification
strategies.desc:
Analyze the mathematical pattern of repeated (scale by a[r]/W, all-reduce, divide by a[r]) cycles to algebraically collapse multiple iterations into fewer operations with adjusted coefficients. Compute effective scaling factors across multiple iterations to reduce from 16 to 8 or fewer all-reduce dispatches. Minimizes communication at the cost of more complex coefficient pre-computation and numerical stability considerations.
